title.narrative: ILO BOUZOUR - Building inclusive markets and decent work in Lebanon
ILO BOUZOUR - inkluderande marknader och förbättrade arbetsvillkor i Libanon.

description.narrative:
1) Increased productivity and decent working conditions in the covered horticulture sector. 2) Farmers and agribusinesses connected to new market opportunities 3) Farmers enabled to use solar energy systems for electricity generation 4) Farmers and small agribusinesses capacitated to better manage their activities and resources
Final beneficiaries will be host communities and refugee workers and specifically those operating in the wider agriculture and renewable energy sectors.
Insatsens mål är att förbättra jordbrukets produktivitet, öppna upp för nya marknader för jordbruksprodukter samt att förbättra arbetsvillkoren..
The project's aim it to increase farmers' productivity, connect agri-business to new markets including decent working conditions.

The below results examples are from the results harvest for year 2025:
Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) tools were developed in partnership with the Ministry of Agriculture, including practical infographics addressing critical safety gaps in greenhouse installation and agricultural work. Improved working conditions for Syrian agricultural workers (majority women) by reducing exposure to heat stress, chemicals and creating more predictable workloads and stable employment periods. The structured recruitment and training model engaged 25 farmers and 348 workers (of which 85% are Syrian workers) leading to improved job quality, safer working conditions, more reliable wages and longer employment durations, especially for Syrian workers.
A contract farming model was piloted with 35 Lebanese farmers, reaching 292 agricultural workers (over 85% Syrian and around 25% women), reducing reliance on informal intermediaries and introducing clearer work arrangements and technical training that improved job quality, wage reliability, and on farm productivity and practices. Productivity gains were achieved across more than 200 farms across multiple agrifood value chains through improved practices, inputs, and technologies. Direct yield increases of 630 per cent were recorded in 47 farms, alongside improved production management and market access.
Despite a lowyield season driven by adverse climate and weather conditions, 102 participating farmers were able to maintain or slightly increase their production, while nonengaged farmers experienced declining yields. This resilience reflects the benefits of structured support, technical guidance, and improved market access provided by the pilot. 60 farmers were trained and supported to implement integrated pest management and meet EU export standards, enhancing farm production quality and market readiness, while also improving job quality for workers.
Climate and environment: Facilitated market uptake of sensor-based irrigation and fertigation systems, reducing water use by 2240% and Fertilizer use by up to 67%. Piloted portable rental solar solutions across 4 agricultural sites, resulting in up to 2 tons of CO emissions reduced per site, alongside reduced energy costs and improved operational reliability.
Increased Local Ownership and Participation: Enabled local manufacturers to deliver affordable upgrades at 30-50% lower cost than market, leading to new orders and continued service provision. Following the rental and testing phase, 3 of the 4 piloted sites transitioned to permanent solar installations, demonstrating strong commercial viability. Climate-smart irrigation provider scaled to 250 farmers, cooperatives, and agribusinesses, with 50 new orders in 2025, demonstrating commercial sustainability.
Results related to social cohesion: Reduced tensions linked to competition over jobs and resources, as productivity gains and market growth expanded economic opportunities for both Lebanese and Syrians. Greenhouse upgrades and installation activities engaged mixed Syrian and Lebanese work teams (around 70% Syrian), creating shared employment opportunities and reducing segmentation in rural labour markets traditionally divided by nationality and gender.
Results connected to Job creation and improvement: Increased productivity and decent working conditions in the covered horticulture sector, 275 jobs created in greenhouse-related activities, of which held by 195 Syrian workers, 945 jobs improved through contract farming arrangements, OSH and climate smart agriculture including 609 Syrian workers, contributing to more predictable workloads and reduced reliance on informal labour intermediaries, enhancing safety, productivity, and working conditions across horticulture value chains.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
